primary_topics: Policy analysis paper on the risks of automated elections for the May 10, 2010 Philippine elections, published April 20, 2010 -- structured as a series of desiderata, realities, problems and legal/political consequences

The HOPE desiderata: Honest, Orderly and Peaceful Elections, if possible automated; reality is limited time, defective automation system, lack of transparency, spotty Comelec preparations, inadequate PCOS testing and voter/teacher orientation

Possible legal consequences of automation failures: failure of elections, failure of proclamation, massive disenfranchisement, massive electoral fraud -- with the critical threshold being whether failures involve more ballots than the margin between the leading presidential candidates

GMA holdover scenario: the constitutional and political conditions required for a holdover; the 'brains and brawns' (SC + AFP + PNP + Church + INC + People Power + US) needed to prop it up; three options (exit gracefully, extend as PM/PM via Cha-cha, or holdover); three preventions
sub_topics: Fundamentals of automation: precinct-specific ballots; precinct-specific PCOS machines; automated counting at precincts; automated transmission; proclamation based on automated results

Automation problems: PCOS or ballots misdelivered; PCOS fail to function; stolen, disabled or burned; erroneously printed ballots; wrong transmission of results; massive disenfranchisements due to long queues
Critical threshold: if automation problems involve more ballots than the margin between the leading presidential candidates, no winner can be proclaimed
Legal consequences: failure of elections (no election actually held); failure of proclamation (no clear winner); massive disenfranchisement; massive electoral fraud (retail and wholesale)

Political consequences: presidential succession by July 1, 2010 (VP, Senate President, Speaker); GMA holdover -- 'not expressly provided by the Constitution but supported by jurisprudence, the latest of which is Seneres vs Comelec (April 16, 2009)'
Brains and brawns for holdover: SC; Armed Forces; PNP; Filipino people including Church, INC and People Organizations; International Community especially the US, to prop up the economy

GMA's three options: (1) prepare to step down -- exit gracefully, name transition team; protect back via House, SC, Sandiganbayan, Ombudsman, Comelec, Military; choose viable candidate; or run for VP; or run for Pampanga Congress seat; (2) extend reign as PM -- Cha-cha via peoples initiative, constituent assembly or con-con; or martial law (only for invasion/rebellion; 60 days; SC reviews factual basis); emergency rule has no constitutional authority; (3) preventions -- HOPE elections, vigilant people and media, People Power, CBCP, Twitter revolt, full-scale revolution
Election timeline: May 10, 2010 to June 30, 2010 = 61 days; 'many things can happen during that period'

Congress role: Congress, not Comelec, canvasses and proclaims President/VP (no later than 30 days after Election Day); in case of tie, majority of all Members of Congress chooses; presidential succession chain under Art. VII Sec. 7
Einstein quote: 'Insanity is committing the same errors and expecting different results'

stances.claim: A GMA holdover after the 2010 elections -- while not expressly provided in the Constitution -- is supported by jurisprudence (Seneres v. Comelec, April 16, 2009). But it requires an extraordinary alignment of 'Brains and Brawns': the SC, AFP, PNP, Church, INC, People Power organizations, and the US (to prop up the economy). Without all of these, a holdover would be unstable.
stances.rhetorical_move: brains-and-brawns-as-holdover-threshold: the enumeration of required institutional support as both a warning and a realistic assessment
stances.confidence: asserted as a constitutional and political analysis

stances.claim: The automation system's problems -- misdelivered PCOS machines, failures, theft, erroneous ballots -- only become catastrophic if they involve more ballots than the margin between the leading presidential candidates. Below that threshold, the problems are localized. This is the governing quantitative threshold for assessing whether 2010 would result in a constitutional crisis.
stances.rhetorical_move: margin-threshold argument: the critical number as the test that separates a manageable problem from a constitutional crisis
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing analytical framework

one_paragraph_summary: Published April 20, 2010 as a structured policy analysis paper on the risks of automated elections for the May 10, 2010 Philippine elections, this document by CJP is organized as a series of headers: desiderata (HOPE: Honest, Orderly and Peaceful Elections, if possible automated), reality (limited time, defective system, spotty Comelec preparations, inadequate PCOS testing), fundamentals of automation (precinct-specific ballots and machines; automated counting, transmission and proclamation), and automation problems (misdelivery, PCOS failures, theft/burning, erroneous ballots, wrong transmissions, long-queue disenfranchisements). The critical threshold: if problems involve more ballots than the margin between the leading presidential candidates, no winner can be proclaimed. Legal consequences: failure of elections, failure of proclamation, massive disenfranchisement, massive electoral fraud. Political consequences: presidential succession (VP, Senate President, Speaker) or GMA holdover -- 'not expressly provided by the Constitution but supported by jurisprudence, the latest of which is Seneres vs. Comelec (April 16, 2009).' For a holdover to work: 'Brains and Brawns' -- SC, AFP, PNP, Church, INC, People Organizations, and the US to prop up the economy. GMA's three options: (1) exit gracefully and protect her back through the House, SC, Sandiganbayan, Ombudsman, Comelec and Military; (2) extend reign via Cha-cha (people's initiative, constituent assembly or con-con), martial law (60 days; Congress can revoke; SC reviews factual basis -- but 'emergency rule has no constitutional authority'); or (3) prevent via HOPE elections, vigilant media and people, People Power, CBCP, Twitter revolt, or full-scale revolution. Timeline: Election Day (May 10) to GMA's term end (June 30) = 61 days. 'Many things can happen during that period.' Closes with Einstein: 'Insanity is committing the same errors and expecting different results.'
